title: Hausdorff measure on (0,1) × M is the product measure
statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k], Φ(s, u) := (s, u_1, …, u_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ u))), π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))), y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0, and assume (MP): for every A ⊆ ℝ^P that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A), where Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2) on ℝ × ℝ^P and L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Hᵐ-null-measurable and countably m-rectifiable with Hᵐ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, and M̃ := {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0, 1)}. Then H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ Hᵐ⌞M).
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), (∀ A : Set (Eucl P), NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) → CountablyRectifiable m A → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) (A ∩ K) < ∞) → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))).restrict {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ A} = Measure.map (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ p.2))) ((volume : Measure ℝ).prod ((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict A))) → ∀ M : Set (Eucl P), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) → CountablyRectifiable m M → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ K) < ∞) → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))).restrict {y : Eucl (P + 1) | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ M ∧ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1} = Measure.map (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ p.2)))) (((volume : Measure ℝ).restrict (Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)).prod ((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M))
